$comment: One authority per concern, written down because it cannot be trusted.
Pi 0.84.4 resolves competing extension handlers silently by load order: for
a `session_before` event every handler result overwrites the previous one,
so two extensions that both answer `session_before_compact` do not conflict
-- the last one loaded simply wins, with no error and no warning. Pi also
exposes no runtime API for enumerating loaded extensions, so an extension
cannot detect the collision from inside either.
That makes a second owner an undetectable failure mode rather than a
degraded one, and it is why this file exists and why conformance asserts
over it. `concerns` is an ARRAY, not an object keyed by concern: an object
cannot represent two owners for one key, which would make the duplicate
check vacuous. The check has to be able to fail.
`status: "unassigned"` is a real entry, not a placeholder to be tidied
away. Naming an unowned concern is what stops it being quietly adopted by

concerns.note: The pinned Pi release. Provider abstraction, the agent loop, sessions, branching and compaction mechanics are ADOPTED from core and not reimplemented.

Pi's own session JSONL. Command Governor does not ship a competing transcript format. Durable Command Governor state lives in an extension-owned sidecar instead, and that sidecar is a separate concern.
Sole reader of pins.json at runtime. Any second version check must consume this module rather than re-deriving the pin.

Decides the pi binary, asserts its version before the process starts, passes --approve for this repository's own settings, and sets PI_SUBAGENTS_TEMP_ROOT to a durable path. ctx.shutdown() is a no-op in print mode, so the launcher is the only place a version refusal is fatal.

The role files are the definitions. They are NOT the enforcement: Pi core has no agents concept, and the `tools` and `model` frontmatter fields bind only whatever extension reads them. See role-loadout-enforcement.
The credential-free tier gates every re-pin. No second suite may claim to verify the pin.

concerns.plannedOwner: pi-subagents@0.62.0 capability ceilings, registered by a Command Governor policy extension
concerns.note: ADR 0008 invariant 6 has no enforcement point in Pi core today. Until a package owns this, harness/agents/*.md restrictions are documentation, and the conformance suite says so rather than implying otherwise.
Selected, reviewed, not installed. Installing it obliges us to set PI_SUBAGENTS_TEMP_ROOT, which bin/cg-pi already does, because the package defaults its durable run state to os.tmpdir().
Gate P4. Transport candidates are capability-gated and replaceable; the interface is fixed now so neither candidate's shape reaches the ledger.

concerns.plannedOwner: a Command Governor extension-owned durable sidecar
concerns.note: Must not be the Pi session JSONL: pi.appendEntry is session-scoped and does not survive as a single authority across fork or switch.

concerns.plannedOwner: exactly one memory package, not yet chosen
concerns.note: The highest-risk unassigned concern. Pi resolves two session_before_compact handlers by load order with no error, so this must be exactly one owner forever. Deferred deliberately: no evaluated candidate satisfies ADR 0007 (c) or (d).
Deferred. Memory is never authority for exact lifecycle, capability, safety or user-owned decision facts (ADR 0008 invariant 5).

ADR 0008 invariant 7 needs a single arbiter. cg-version-guard registers a tool_call handler today, but only to fail closed on an unverified runtime -- it is not a policy gate and must not become one by accretion.
